title: Width counter update for one literal
statement: Let $\ell=(v,b)$ be a literal with variable index $v\in\mathbb{N}$ and polarity bit $b\in\{0,1\}$, let $c\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and let $g$ be a Boolean flag. Folding the width-pass transition over the binary encoding of $\ell$, starting in state $1$ with counter $c$ and flag $g$, ends in state $1$ with counter $\min(c+1,3)$ and flag $g\wedge[c<3]$.
hypotheses_covered: $\ell$ is a literal over natural-number-indexed variables
replaced:
Let $\ell$ be a literal, $c \in \{0,1,2,3\}$ a counter value, and $g$ a Boolean
flag. Folding the width-pass transition over the serialization of $\ell$, from the
clause position with counter $c$ and flag $g$, returns the clause position with
counter $\min(c + 1, 3)$ and flag $g \wedge [c < 3]$, independently of the
variable index and polarity of $\ell$.
